after.statement: The factsheet describes a broad climatic range for kermes oak, including occurrence around 200 mm annual rainfall at Cabo de Gata, while reporting 400-800 mm as its more favourable rainfall context.

after.context: Vegetation discussion on FOREST-003 PDF page 2; descriptive community occurrence.
limitations: Co-occurrence does not establish a mandatory planting mixture, planting distance or beneath-crown compatibility.

after.statement: The factsheet lists kermes oak with thermophilous vegetation including carob, lentisk, palmetto and wild olive, among other community contexts.

limitations: The source list is not a complete planting recipe. Its climatic terminology must not be used to classify a parcel automatically.
after.statement: The factsheet lists a semi-arid Quercus coccifera vegetation series under the Latin name Rhamno lycioidis-Querceto cocciferae sigmetum.

after.context: Distribution and substrate descriptions on PDF pages 1-2.
limitations: Broad occurrence does not demonstrate adequate rootable volume, water availability or performance at a proposed planting point.
after.statement: The factsheet reports kermes oak on dry, stony ground, commonly calcareous, while also describing acidic substrates and a range of soil types.

after.context: The two descriptions refer to the same warm-series entry on FOREST-003 PDF page 3; they remain unresolved together.
limitations: The retained Designer display label is an existing interpretation, not a resolution of this source tension. Further vegetation-taxonomy review is required.
after.statement: That same warm-series entry gives the parenthesized Latin label Bupleuro gibraltarii-Pistacieto lentisci, naming lentisk rather than repeating the prose Quercus label.

after.context: The two descriptions refer to the same warm-series entry on FOREST-003 PDF page 3; they remain unresolved together.

after.context: Kermes oak is already an optional member of the native MR2 Designer palette. This relationship exposes that retained project association.
limitations: Optional membership does not select a plant, prescribe a mixture or establish ecological or beneath-crown suitability.

after.explanation: The warm-series line uses coscoja/Quercus coccifera in prose and Bupleuro-Pistacieto lentisci in its Latin label. Preserve both descriptions pending vegetation-series review; select neither as a corrected source identity.
limitations: Bounded to the inspected line and existing research context. This does not invalidate every vegetation-series entry in the factsheet.

value.description: designer-v3.place_new implements defaults.placement: the eight registered woodland companions use all plotted planned tree crowns, balanced by association count and stable tree ID. Candidates are uniform by area, seed-stable and bounded, with 1 m centre clearance. Other shrubs/grasses use open ground; custom plants independent. Existing vegetation is an obstacle. value.limitations: Woodland co-occurrence does not prove beneath-crown compatibility with every tree. Clearance, grouping, seed and attempts are geometric project assumptions. Failed placements retain counts and costs. Only new instances are generated. Manual movement detaches shrubs; tree movement translates associated offsets. No sun, wind, soil or mycelial suitability model.
